d: to control oneself by thorough discipline
to exercise complete control over one’s desires and actions
to exercise complete control over one’s desires and actions
(derivative of {L:ἐγκρατεύομαι<SDBG:ἐγκρατεύομαι:000000>} ‘to exercise self-control,’ {D:88.83}) pertaining to exercising self-control
(derivative of {L:ἀκρασία<SDBG:ἀκρασία:000000>} ‘lack of self-control,’ {D:88.91}) pertaining to lacking self-control
(derivative of {L:νήφω<SDBG:νήφω:000001>}[b] ‘to be restrained,’ {D:88.86}) pertaining to behaving in a sober, restrained manner
(a figurative extension of meaning of νήφω ‘to be sober,’ in the sense of ‘not being drunk,’ probably not occurring in the NT) to behave with restraint and moderation, thus not permitting excess

(a figurative extension of meaning of ὑπωπιάζω ‘to strike the eye,’ not occurring in the NT) to keep one’s body under complete control, with the implication of rough treatment given to the body, possibly as an aspect of discipline (a meaning evidently taken from the language of prize-fighting)
(a figurative extension of meaning of χαλιναγωγέω ‘to control with bit or bridle,’ not occurring in the NT) to exercise close control over some function
severe self-control, suggesting an ascetic and unsparing attitude
